target: Nos echamos de menos.
english: We miss each other.
tip: The nos is what makes it mutual: echamos de menos alone means we miss (someone). Add nos and the missing points both ways – we miss each other.

target: Vengo por la mañana.
english: I come in the morning.
tip: Not 'for the morning' – with parts of the day, por just means 'in'. "Vengo por la mañana" = I come in the morning: a loose timeframe, nothing traded.

target: Te lo explico ahora.
english: I'll explain it to you now.
tip: Double pronouns: indirect + direct. "Te lo dije" = I told it to you. Indirect pronoun (te) goes first, then direct (lo).

target: Nos vamos a las ocho.
english: We're leaving at eight.
tip: Ir = go, irse = leave. The "Nos" in "Nos vamos" isn't 'us' – it flips go into depart: we're off at eight, destination irrelevant.

target: Firme aquí abajo, por favor.
english: Sign here below, please.
tip: "Firme" isn't a typo for firma – that final -e is the usted command. Formal orders swap the vowel: firme, pase, disculpe. The -a form would sound chummy.

target: Él se equivocó de puerta.
english: He went through the wrong door.
tip: You don't 'go through the wrong door' – you mistake yourself OF door: "se equivocó de puerta". Equivocarse de + bare noun, no article, for any wrong-X.

target: Me quedo en casa esta noche.
english: I'm staying home tonight.
tip: "Quedarse" = to stay/remain. Different from "quedar" (to arrange to meet). "Me quedé en casa" = I stayed home.

target: Se me olvidó enviar el correo.
english: I forgot to send the email.
tip: Se me olvidó: accidental se construction – 'it slipped my mind'.

target: Le dije que viniera a las tres.
english: I told him to come at three.
tip: Because dije is past, the subjunctive time-travels with it: viniera, not venga. Spanish matches the order's tense to when you gave it.

target: No abras la ventana, hace mucho frío.
english: Don't open the window, it's very cold.
tip: Telling someone NOT to do it changes the verb: ¡abre! = open!, but "No abras" = don't open. Negative tú commands borrow the subjunctive form.

target: Se nos olvidó cerrar la puerta con llave.
english: We forgot to lock the door.
tip: Olvidársele – unplanned event: se nos olvidó – we forgot (accidentally).

target: Ella se quita los zapatos al llegar a casa.
english: She takes off her shoes when she gets home.
tip: Why "los zapatos", not sus zapatos? The "se quita" already says whose they are – Spanish drops 'her' with clothes and body parts.

target: Pagué veinte euros por el libro.
english: I paid twenty euros for the book.
tip: "Por" = in exchange for: "Lo compré por diez euros." Por for what you pay or trade.

target: La propuesta se la envié al director ayer.
english: I sent the proposal to the director yesterday.
tip: Why "se la envié", never 'le la'? Two l-pronouns can't touch: le turns into se before lo/la. The se here is the director, not a reflexive.

target: Suele llegar tarde los lunes por el trafico.
english: He usually arrives late on Mondays due to traffic.
tip: 'Suele' is from soler: soler + infinitive = to usually do something (habitual).

target: Mi hija se viste sola desde los cuatro años.
english: My daughter has been able to dress herself since she was four.
tip: "desde los cuatro años" + plain present = 'has dressed herself since four'. Spanish uses now-tense for still-true situations – no 'has been' machinery.

target: Ella tiene alergia al polen y le lloran los ojos.
english: She is allergic to pollen and her eyes water.
tip: Her eyes act on their own: "le lloran los ojos" = 'the eyes cry to her'. Spanish hands the person a le and lets the body part be the subject.

target: La forma en que habla me recuerda a mi abuelo.
english: The way he speaks reminds me of my grandfather.
tip: "En que" = in which/on which: "El día en que llegó" = The day on which he arrived. Preposition + que for things.

target: Le cuesta levantarse temprano.
english: He has a hard time getting up early.
tip: Costar prices effort, not just money: Le cuesta levantarse = getting up 'costs him'. The struggler is le, the struggle is the subject – a gustar-style flip.

target: Este regalo es para ti.
english: This gift is for you.
tip: "Para" = for (recipient): "Es para ti." Para marks who receives something.

target: La casa huele a comida.
english: The house smells like food.
tip: Oler always takes a, never como: "huele a comida" is literally 'smells to food'. The a marks the source of the smell.

target: Mi hermano toca la guitarra.
english: My brother plays the guitar.
tip: Tocar means touch – Spanish speakers literally 'touch the guitar'. And it's always la guitarra with the article, never 'toca guitarra' like English 'plays guitar'.

target: Se las envié esta mañana.
english: I sent them to her this morning.
tip: Two l-pronouns can't touch: 'le las envié' is illegal, so le morphs into se – Se las envié. That se isn't reflexive, it's le in disguise.

target: Necesito terminarlo para el viernes.
english: I need to finish it by Friday.
tip: Deadline = para, never por: para el viernes means done BY Friday. Por el viernes would drift toward 'around Friday' – your boss wants para.

target: Me gustaría reservar una habitación.
english: I would like to book a room.
tip: "Me gustaría" + infinitive – polite way to express a wish.

target: No puedo ir por el trabajo.
english: I can't go because of work.
tip: "Por" = because of. Expresses the cause or obstacle: "No salimos por la lluvia" (We didn't go out because of the rain).

target: Quiero que mis hijos sean felices.
english: I want my children to be happy.
tip: Quiero que flips the next verb to subjunctive: sean, not son. You're wishing happiness on them, not reporting it – Spanish marks that gap in the verb itself.

target: Me di cuenta del error a tiempo.
english: I noticed the error in time.
tip: Don't reach for 'realizar' – that means to carry out. To notice/realize is darse cuenta: Me di cuenta del error, literally 'I gave myself account'.

target: Ella lleva a sus hijos al colegio.
english: She takes her children to school.
tip: Lleva = takes AWAY from where you are; trae = brings toward you. She lleva a sus hijos to school because the speaker isn't standing at the school.

target: Me quedé en casa por la lluvia.
english: I stayed home because of the rain.
tip: "Por" = because of. Expresses what caused something: "Lo hice por ti" (I did it because of you).
